comment: Sorry for the late answer. The Salvation Army Church across the alley from my house has leased part of their property to Google Fiber. Understand I love Google Fiber, I have it. However early to late the trucks and equipment make so much noise it comes into our house. My husband and I have a home recording studio that is pretty well insulated but when they move dirt around and their equipment is mixing "imprecise" (not sure that is what they are doing) we have to stop work and wait until they are gone for a few hours. Of course there is no peace in our once quite yard and neighborhood where we used to enjoy outside activity. I'm not sure if this make a lot of sense but I do have recorded video of how loud it is when they work. I have lived in Poplar Grove for 38 years so I have a fair comparison. The neighborhood has single family dwellings and a small apartment nearby with some small businesses. Construction site noise is not too compatible with our homes. The site is on 900 West between 400 and 500 South. I live on Post Street across the alley. I would like to know who I can chat with about how long this will continue. So far about two years but it's getting to be a bigger operation."

Hi Dan, I hope all is well with you and your family. I am writing to let you know that I strongly support The Other Side Village. It is a cause I feel strongly about. All people deserve shelter even if they can't obtain it on their own. I hope that you will support The Other Side Village project in the upcoming City Council vote. Thank you for serving on the city council. Sincerely your neighbor and friend, April Mills Sent from my iPhone

Hello Alejandro, My name is Daniel Fale, and my partner Graig Griffin and I have been working with the Carter family who owns multiple parcels (with businesses) adjacent to the proposed rezone at 1850w Indiana Avenue and 1965W 500S (their parcels being 1802-1818 W Indiana Ave). As our client's parcels of land, as well as the adjacent proposed rezone fall under District 2, Poplar Grove, we wanted to reach out to you-as our council member-to ensure we are kept in the loop with regard to all coming work meetings/or other discussions surrounding the proposed rezone. On 10-27-21, we did voice support with concerns related to the rezone at the Planning Committee Meeting. Ultimately the following was decided and has been copied and pasted directly from the 10-27-21 Minutes: "The motion moved forward with the friendly amendment accepted, it is restated here: Salt Lake City Planning Commission October 27, 2021 Page 12 Commissioner Brenda Scheer stated, Based on the findings and analysis in the staff report, testimony, and discussion at the public hearing, I move that the Planning Commission recommend that the City Council approve the proposed Zoning Map Amendment, file PLNPCM2021-00787 for the properties located at 1850 W Indiana Avenue and 1965 West 500 South respectively, proposed zone change from the PL (Public Lands) zoning district to the FB-UN2 (Form Based Urban Neighborhood) zoning district with the following recommendation: Whereas the community and the public should have the opportunity to plan the neighborhood with the large and potentially impactful project. We recommend that the Council ask the City staff to work with the applicant, businesses, and the community to prepare a development agreement prior to conveying the property. This plan needs to look at infrastructure, including transportation, services, Commercial development, and the buffering and protection of the existing business and the needs of the nearby residents. Commissioners Maurine Bachman, Mike Christensen, Andra Ghent, Sara Urquhart, Andres Paredes, Jon Lee, and Brenda Scheer voted "yes". Commissioner Aimee Burrows voted "no". The motion passed with 7 "yes" and 1 "no". The next step sounds as though it is a "work session" and we would like to know how we can be involved to ensure that our client's voice-concern is reiterated/heard.
